What happened each year, and how often
Tap a disaster type to switch it on or off. Hover a bar for that year’s counts. The table below shows the same numbers by type.

Source: EM-DAT (CRED, UCLouvain), processed by Our World in Data. A disaster is recorded when it causes 10+ deaths, affects 100+ people, or triggers an emergency declaration or a call for international aid. EM-DAT counts tsunamis under earthquakes. Years before 2000 are left out because records are incomplete.
Which countries were hit hardest, and by what
Darker countries had more disaster deaths in 2000–2025. The symbol on a country is its deadliest disaster type. Tap a country to open its own map.

Sources: cumulative deaths from EM-DAT / Our World in Data. When Apophis comes close, and how close
Apophis (99942) is an asteroid about 340 m across, not a comet. Each dot is an approach and its distance; the vertical line is the computed uncertainty. Lower means closer to Earth.
Apophis passes about 38,000 km from Earth’s centre, inside the ring of geostationary satellites. After radar observations in 2021, NASA said there is
no impact risk for at least 100 years
Distances are NASA/JPL computed values from Earth’s centre. The view uses a log scale, so nearer distances are magnified. The red band is the uncertainty range.

Sources: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database close-approach data (orbit solution 220); NASA statement, March 2021. Distances are from Earth’s centre. Earth’s gravity changes the orbit in 2029, so uncertainty grows for later dates.
